traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Dilleniaceae: leaves usually alternate, rarely opposite; leaves simple; margins entire or serrate; veins single, pinnate or palmate; leaves deciduous; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes usually none, sometimes basal; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually woody, rarely herbaceous; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule, follicle, achene or aggregate; stamens 1 to 150; carpels (1-) 2 to 7 (-20). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 297, family Dilleniaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.vernation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 297, family Dilleniaceae: vernation conduplicate; read as "conduplicate".

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Hibbertia (read 2026-10-17; ~400 spp): flowers mostly single in leaf axils or at shoot tips. Wikipedia Dillenia (read 2026-10-17; 60 spp): flowers single or in terminal racemes (raceme added). Cymes and panicles are left to the smaller climbing genera (Tetracera and allies), far fewer species. Re-ranks the earlier value, from floral-diagrams, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Weighted by genus: Wikipedia Hibbertia (read 2026-10-17; about 400 spp, the bulk of a family Britannica puts at 11 genera) gives smooth leaf edges, only rarely toothed or lobed. Toothed blades belong to the much smaller tree and liana genera (Dillenia, 60 spp per Wikipedia/POWO; Tetracera and the neotropical lianas), so entire margins cover well over half the species.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Hibbertia (read 2026-10-17; ~400 spp, the large majority of the family): fruit of follicles holding arillate seeds. Dillenia (60 spp, Wikipedia read the same day: 5-20 free carpels) gives the clustered, sepal-wrapped aggregate; capsule and achene stay as minor states from the old value.
